Here are practical things to look for when shopping for a new electric guitar (based on what you’ve been discussing):

- Body & construction: note the body shape and build (e.g., Strat-style contoured bolt‑on vs Les Paul single‑cutaway with set neck). That affects comfort, tone, and sustain.
- Neck & feel: try different neck profiles and fretboard feels to see what’s comfortable for your hand. Neck construction (bolt‑on vs set) changes feel and resonance.
- Pickups and electronics: different pickup types give very different tones. If you want more tonal options, consider guitars with coil‑tap/coil‑split or humbucker/single‑coil switching.
- String gauge & tuning needs: if you plan alternate tunings (like open D), heavier strings can help the instrument feel and sound better at lower tensions.
- Setup, action & intonation: check the action, fret buzzing, and whether the guitar intonates properly up the neck — these greatly affect playability. Ask if the store can do a quick setup or demo with adjustments.
- Playability for your style: test chords, riffs and any specific parts you play (e.g., fingerpicking or acoustic‑like parts) to ensure the guitar responds well to your technique.
- Hardware quality: check the bridge, tuners, and overall build quality for stability and sustain.
- Try amps and effects: plug the guitar into an amp and try settings and tones you’d actually use so you hear how pickups and wood interact with your sound.

Bring a list of songs/parts you play and spend time playing each candidate rather than relying on specs alone — feel and tone in your hands matter most.
